headline: Highest risk is medium: Flowise can write shared files and use broad egress, while spring-integration-samples is non-networked and unverified, so interaction risks are limited but not absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write server filesystem and run browser/tool nodes, so if spring-integration-samples content is manually copied into a flow or shared file, prompt injection is possible. B has no network egress and no shared channel is documented, so the bridge is weak and likely manual.
conditions: IF operators copy B-generated text into a Flowise prompt or file input, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is introduced, attacker-controlled content can reach Flowise parsing.
mitigations: Keep B outputs out of Flowise prompt fields.
Use a read-only handoff file format with explicit delimiters.
Disable browser/tool nodes for untrusted content paths.
Review any copied snippets before pasting into Flowise.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files, so sensitive data could be exposed if B is placed in the same workspace. B itself has network_egress none, so it is not a likely exfiltration source; the main risk is local workspace leakage rather than outbound transmission.
conditions: IF B artifacts are stored in the same server filesystem as Flowise chatflow files, leakage is possible.
IF Flowise flows ingest uploaded files containing sensitive data, those contents may be exposed in outputs or logs.
mitigations: Store B artifacts outside Flowise's workspace.
Restrict file upload paths to a dedicated directory.
Redact secrets before importing content into Flowise.
Audit logs for accidental inclusion of file contents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise has broad filesystem write and shared server-datastore state across instances, while B is unverified and its runtime/write behavior is not documented. If both touch the same mutable workspace, conflicts can occur; uncertainty about B's write surface pushes this above low.
conditions: IF B writes to the same directory or datastore as Flowise, concurrent mutation conflicts can occur.
IF multiple Flowise instances share the same server datastore without locking, state races are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files.
Take a backup before running both agents.
Serialize updates to shared datastore entries.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is an orchestration layer that can pass outputs into downstream tools, so if B's outputs are treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into actions or generated work products. B is a sample integration repo with no runtime safeguards documented, so verification gaps remain.
conditions: IF Flowise feeds B-derived text into downstream tools without validation, errors can propagate.
IF operators rely on B outputs as facts, downstream actions may be incorrect.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before downstream actions.
Require source citations for any factual output.
Compare B outputs against an independent check.
Disable auto-execution of tool actions from imported text.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, retention, or regulated-data mismatch is documented for either agent. Flowise handles model keys and tool credentials, while B has no data classes touched; absent evidence of regulated data flow, compliance risk is limited but should be checked if sensitive data is introduced.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Flowise flows, compliance obligations may apply.
IF B is used to process personal data, retention and residency controls must be verified.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair.
Document data categories before deployment.
Review retention settings in Flowise.
Confirm hosting region for any model providers.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data paths.
